title: Anatomical hop count predicted response probability but not fitted response timing in the C. elegans signal propagation atlas; the kernel times repeated poorly across mirror pairs
abstract: We tested if responses to optogenetic stimulation in the C. elegans head need more time when the shortest anatomical path has more synaptic steps (hops). We used the Randi et al. 2023 signal propagation atlas and the union of four anatomical maps (White 1986 adult and L4, Witvliet 2021 adults 7 and 8). We kept 178 head neurons that have synapses in the maps. From each fitted transfer kernel of a responding pair (q < 0.05) we measured peak time, rise time and half-mass time. In wild-type animals, 10.2% of directly connected pairs responded and 4.7% of indirect pairs responded. With fixed effects for the stimulated and responding neurons, a direct connection added 5.5 percentage points (95% CI 3.7 to 7.2; 15,384 pairs). In 1,000 degree-preserving rewired maps, the direct-pair response rate was 5.6% (4.7 to 6.5%). Thus the specific wiring predicted response occurrence. Fitted timing did not follow the wiring. With the same fixed effects, the direct-to-indirect ratio of half-mass time was 0.92 (0.76 to 1.12; 718 pairs). Peak and rise times also gave coefficients near zero. Median peak times (0.44 s) were less than one 0.5 s imaging frame. Kernel times repeated poorly: for 87 left-right mirror pairs, Spearman rho was 0.16 (-0.06 to 0.37) for half-mass time and 0.02 for peak time, but 0.46 (0.25 to 0.64) for response amplitude. In unc-31 mutants (no dense-core vesicle release), the direct-connection effect on response probability was smaller (+2.0 points, 0.0 to 3.9), and timing again showed no hop-count effect. Limitations: kernel fits at 2 volumes/s with a calcium indicator, trial-averaged kernels, a permissive union of maps, unmapped pharyngeal and ventral cord neurons, and a rewired null that treats pairs as independent. Atlas kernel times are not reliable pair-specific delay measurements at this resolution.

The wild-type timing value is outside the null range, but its cluster bootstrap interval includes zero and the fixed-effects model shows no effect.
